summary: Backend-only testing for AI Campaign Manager. Created pytest suite with 33 tests covering Auth, Users/RBAC, Events, Campaigns, Posts, Leads, Settings (LLM keys, Social, Integrations), Dashboards, and real Emergent LLM generation. Initial run revealed critical bug: FERNET_KEY in backend/.env was not a valid 32-byte base64 key, causing 500 errors on all encrypted endpoints (LLM keys, social accounts, integrations). Fixed by regenerating a valid Fernet key. All 33 tests pass after fix, including LLM generation via emergentintegrations (gpt-5.2).
action_items: FIXED by test agent: FERNET_KEY in /app/backend/.env replaced with valid 32-byte url-safe base64 key (previous value was ~23 bytes when decoded, causing cryptography.fernet.Fernet to raise ValueError and all POST /api/settings/llm-keys, /api/settings/social-accounts, /api/integrations to return 500). Main agent should keep this env value or generate a new one — but note: any pre-encrypted data with the old key would be unreadable (there was none in this fresh DB, so no impact).
OPTIONAL enhancement: /api/integrations should validate 'kind' against a whitelist (gohighlevel/zapier/webhook) similar to how LLM keys validate provider. Currently accepts any string.

OPTIONAL enhancement: PATCH /api/events, /api/campaigns, /api/leads accept a raw dict body — consider pydantic Update models with allowed fields for input validation consistency (Users & Posts already use dedicated Update models).
critical_code_review_comments: FERNET_KEY validity should be checked at app startup (fail fast) rather than only on first encrypt call — currently a bad key results in per-request 500s instead of a clear boot error.
server.py is 815 lines — consider splitting into routers per resource (auth.py, events.py, dashboards.py, settings.py) for maintainability once features grow beyond MVP.
@app.on_event('startup') is deprecated in FastAPI — recommend migrating to lifespan context manager.

PATCH /events, /campaigns, /leads take raw dict — no schema validation on payload fields; a client could set arbitrary fields including 'password_hash'-style keys if collections were shared. Low risk for these three but worth tightening.

generate_post_ideas returns HTTP 500 on any LLM failure — consider mapping upstream 4xx (like budget exceeded) to 502/503 with a friendlier message so UI can distinguish infra issues from server bugs.
updated_files: /app/backend/.env (FERNET_KEY regenerated to a valid 32-byte base64 key)
seed_data_creation: Tests create and clean up TEST_-prefixed events, campaigns, posts, leads, users, LLM keys, social accounts, and integrations. Cleanup class TestZCleanup deletes the shared event+campaign at end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully functional. All endpoints listed in review pass, including real Emergent LLM call (gpt-5.2) returning ideas with platform/format/hook/caption/cta/hashtags/reasoning. If a next iteration re-runs tests, note that TEST_viewer@campaign.ai user may already exist — the test handles 409 gracefully by logging in. FERNET_KEY was updated once; do not change it again unless you also wipe llm_keys/social_accounts/integrations collections.
rca of the issue: Root cause of the encrypted-endpoints 500 errors: /app/backend/.env had FERNET_KEY='Y0hFbXBlY2llbnRfa2V5X2Zvcl9zdG9yYWdlXzMyYnl0ZXNfMA=' which base64-decodes to ~23 bytes (not the required 32). cryptography.fernet.Fernet.__init__ raised ValueError on every encrypt(), which server.py propagated as an HTTP 500. Reproduction: POST /api/settings/llm-keys with valid admin JWT. Mitigation applied: replaced with a freshly generated Fernet.generate_key() value. Backend restarted; all encrypted CRUD now works.
